title: HIAS was founded in New York to help Jewish refugees, and today helps refugees of every religion and nationality

trailer.text: HIAS describes itself as an international Jewish humanitarian organization, and according to the organization, the Jewish community founded it in New York in the '80s of the 19th century.
The aim was to help Jews from Eastern Europe who had fled antisemitic persecution.
HIAS estimates that it has helped more than 4.5 million people escape persecution.
According to the organization, today it helps refugees and displaced people around the world, regardless of religion, nationality or ethnicity.
According to HIAS, it helps refugees not because they are Jewish, but because HIAS is Jewish.

paragraphs.text: According to Mark Hetfield, in 1881 Tsar Alexander II was assassinated.
He says the assassination led to a surge of antisemitism, and many Jews emigrated to the United States.
According to Encyclopaedia Judaica, that same year in New York a temporary committee for the relief of Russian emigrants founded the Hebrew Emigrant Aid Society.
The committee was meant to help Jews escaping Czarist Russia.
According to the Holocaust Encyclopedia, the place was the Lower East Side of Manhattan.
According to HIAS, in 1902 community members gathered in a shop on the Lower East Side and started a group.
According to the Center for Jewish History, this was a mutual aid society in the store of Max Meyerson, and its name was soon changed to Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society.
According to HIAS, the organization was formally incorporated in 1903.

stations.title: Ellis Island: translation, screenings and a kosher kitchen

paragraphs.text: According to HIAS, in 1904 a bureau was set up on Ellis Island.
The bureau helped new arrivals with translation, with medical screenings and with preventing deportation.
On Ellis Island HIAS also opened a kosher kitchen.
According to Hetfield, the organization maintained it throughout its history.

According to the Holocaust Encyclopedia, during World War II and the Holocaust, HIAS staff met refugee ships at ports of entry to the United States and assisted those who were seeking relatives or friends.
They helped those who were seeking relatives or friends.
According to Hetfield, among the Titanic survivors HIAS helped everyone, regardless of nationality or religion.

stations.title: The gates closed, and the Holocaust drew near

paragraphs.text: According to HIAS, the Emergency Quota Act of 1921 and the National Origins Act of 1924 meant that few Jewish refugees were admitted to the United States.
In response, HIAS and other organizations set up a European arm called HICEM.
According to the Holocaust Encyclopedia, in summer 1943 HIAS launched a program to register relatives of refugees.
The program helped Americans find out what had happened to their relatives.
Mark Hetfield: 22 employees

stations.title: After the war: emptying the camps

paragraphs.text: According to HIAS, after the war it helped evacuate the Displaced Persons camps in Europe.
According to the Holocaust Encyclopedia, the displaced persons received new homes in the United States, Canada, Australia and South America.
According to HIAS, on August 24, 1954, HIAS merged with USNA and with the migration service of the Joint.
The aim was to avoid duplication in the Jewish community's efforts.
According to HIAS, in 1965 U.S. lawmakers replaced the National Origins Act with new legislation.
According to the organization, this happened thanks to strong advocacy by it and by others.

stations.title: From Vietnam, the Soviet Union and Ethiopia

paragraphs.text: According to the Center for Jewish History, in 1975 HIAS found new homes for 3,600 refugees from Southeast Asia, at the request of the State Department.
They settled in 150 communities in 38 U.S. states.
According to HIAS, more than 400,000 Jews from the former Soviet Union migrated with its assistance through Vienna and Rome.
Among those HIAS assisted was Sergey Brin, later a co-founder of Google, who emigrated with his family from the Soviet Union to the United States at the age of six.
According to HIAS, in 1977 it helped evacuate the Jews of Ethiopia.
The evacuation culminated in several dramatic airlifts to Israel.

stations.title: For every refugee, because we are Jewish

paragraphs.text: According to the Holocaust Encyclopedia, HIAS says: we used to welcome refugees because they were Jewish, and today we welcome refugees because we are Jewish.

According to Hetfield, by the beginning of the 21st century Jews had benefited from the legal protections of the 1951 Refugee Convention, from the establishment of the State of Israel and, finally, from the lifting of emigration and religious restrictions in the Soviet bloc, and these developments allowed HIAS to work with UNHCR and other partners to protect all members of humanity, regardless of their ethnicity or religion.
According to HIAS, its mission is to provide vital services to refugees and asylum seekers and to advance their rights, based on Jewish values and history.
According to HIAS, it opened an office in Ecuador in 2003, following the refugee crisis caused by the conflict in Colombia.
In 2005 it arrived in Chad because of the genocide in Darfur, and over two decades it helped hundreds of thousands of refugees there.
In 2016 it opened an office on the island of Lesvos in Greece, because of the civil war in Syria.
According to HIAS, after the fall of Kabul in 2021 and the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, it mobilized its networks.
It resettled Afghans and provided humanitarian aid to refugees from Ukraine.

According to HIAS, in response to the attack of October 7, 2023 and the war in Gaza, HIAS Israel mobilized to support hundreds of thousands of displaced people, providing emergency protection services, shelter access, cash assistance, food and household items, and mental health care.

According to the second edition of the Encyclopaedia Judaica, at the time the entry was written about 30 percent of the HIAS budget came from the U.S. Department of State, and the remainder from private donations.
According to the Holocaust Encyclopedia, in 2018 HIAS was one of nine agencies the State Department worked with to resettle refugees.
According to HIAS, in 2025, 117 million people remained displaced around the world.
According to Religion News Service, nearly 300 synagogues in the United States and Canada took part in National Refugee Shabbat on October 19–20, 2018.
According to Bill Swersey of HIAS, about 425 congregations committed to help refugees in some way.
According to the Holocaust Encyclopedia, on October 27, 2018, a white supremacist murdered 11 Jews at the Tree of Life Synagogue in Pittsburgh.
Before that, he posted lies online about HIAS's work on behalf of refugees.

According to a Religion News Service report shortly after the shooting in October 2018, Bowers had at that point been charged with 29 counts, including obstructing the free exercise of religious beliefs, a hate crime that can carry the death penalty.
According to Religion News Service, Tucker Carlson has argued since at least 2014 that refugees have no moral right to American tax dollars.
He says it is “appalling” that faith groups use federal money to resettle refugees.

According to the same source, groups such as Refugee Resettlement Watch have spent years attacking immigration, and the Southern Poverty Law Center lists Refugee Resettlement Watch as an anti-Muslim hate group.
In 1981 the Jewish Defense League took over the main offices of HIAS in Manhattan.
It protested the "lack of action" to rescue Ethiopian Jews.
According to Encyclopaedia Judaica, in the 1980s there were tensions between HIAS and the Israeli government over whether to help Soviet Jews emigrate to countries other than Israel.

claims.text: HIAS מגדירה את עצמה ארגון הומניטרי יהודי בינלאומי שהתמודד עם אתגרים קשים רבים העומדים בפני עקורים לאורך תולדותיה.
claims.quote: We’re an international Jewish humanitarian organization that has confronted and overcome many formidable challenges facing displaced people throughout our history.

claims.text: לפי HIAS, הקהילה היהודית ייסדה את הארגון בשנות ה-80 של המאה ה-19 בעיר ניו יורק, שער ההגירה לאמריקה.
claims.quote: In the 1880s, the Jewish community founded HIAS (originally the Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society) in New York City, the immigrant gateway to America.

claims.text: לפי הערכת HIAS, היא סייעה ליותר מ-4.5 מיליון בני אדם להימלט מרדיפות.
claims.quote: HIAS estimates that it has helped more than 4.5 million people escape persecution.

claims.text: לפי HIAS, כיום היא מסייעת לפליטים ולעקורים ברחבי העולם בלי קשר לדתם, ללאומיותם או למוצאם האתני.
claims.quote: HIAS now helps refugees and displaced people around the world, regardless of their religion, nationality, or ethnicity.

claims.text: לפי HIAS, דרך הפעולה שלה היא לסייע לפליטים לא משום שהם יהודים אלא משום ש-HIAS היא יהודית.
claims.quote: This became HIAS’ way of working; assisting refugees not because they are Jewish, but because HIAS is Jewish.

claims.text: לפי HIAS, רשת ההושבה שלה בארצות הברית כוללת 30 אזורי מטרופולין, ויותר מ-475 בתי כנסת ברשת שלה.
claims.quote: In the United States, our refugee resettlement network grew to include 30 metropolitan areas across the country.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית השואה, HIAS נוסדה בניו יורק, בלואר איסט סייד של מנהטן, ב-1881.
claims.quote: HIAS has been one of the most influential aid organizations for immigrants and refugees since its founding in New York City, on the Lower East Side of Manhattan, in 1881.

claims.text: לפי הטפילד, ב-1881 נרצח הצאר אלכסנדר השני, דבר שהוביל לגל אנטישמיות ולהגירת יהודים רבים לארצות הברית.
claims.quote: 1881 was also the year that Russia's Tsar Alexander II was assassinated, which led to a surge of anti-semitism and resulted in many Jews crossing the Atlantic

claims.text: לפי יודאיקה, הארגון נוסד בניו יורק ב-1881 כאשר ועדה זמנית לסיוע למהגרים רוסים, שנועדה לעזור ליהודים הנמלטים מרוסיה הצארית, הקימה את האגודה העברית לסיוע למהגרים.
claims.quote: hias was founded in New York City in 1881, when the Russian Emigrant Relief Committee, a temporary body established to help Jews escaping Czarist Russia

claims.text: לפי HIAS, ב-1902 התכנסו אנשי קהילה בחנות בלואר איסט סייד והקימו קבוצה שנודעה בהמשך בשם Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society.
claims.quote: In 1902, community members gathered in a shop on the Lower East Side and started a group that would come to be known as the Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society.

claims.text: לפי מרכז ההיסטוריה היהודית, ב-3 בדצמבר 1902 אורגנה אגודת עזרה הדדית בחנותו של מקס מאיירסון, ושמה שונה במהרה ל-Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society.
claims.quote: was organized in the store of Max Meyerson. The name was soon changed to Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society, known as HIAS

claims.text: לפי HIAS, הארגון התאגד רשמית כ-Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society ב-1903, כהמשך לארגונים קודמים שפעלו בשנות ה-80 וה-90 של המאה ה-19.
claims.quote: Though the organization was formally incorporated as the Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society in 1903, that founding moment represented a continuation of several predecessor organizations

claims.text: לפי HIAS, ב-1904 הוקמה לשכה באליס איילנד שסייעה לבאים חדשים בתרגום, בבדיקות רפואיות ובמניעת גירושים.
claims.quote: Organizers set up a bureau on Ellis Island in 1904 to assist new arrivals, providing translation services, guiding immigrants through medical screenings

claims.text: לפי מרכז ההיסטוריה היהודית, בסביבות 1910 פתחה HIAS מטבח כשר באליס איילנד.
claims.quote: Circa 1910, HIAS opens kosher kitchen on Ellis Island.

claims.quote: So, in 1911, HIAS set up a kosher kitchen on Ellis Island, which it maintained throughout its history.

claims.quote: Of course, HIAS helped everyone regardless of their nationality or faith.

claims.quote: Because of the Emergency Quota Act of 1921 and the subsequent National Origins Act of 1924, few Jewish refugees were admitted to the United States.

claims.text: לפי HIAS, בתגובה למכסות היא החליטה לפעול בשותפות עם ארגונים נוספים כדי להקים זרוע אירופית בשם HICEM.
claims.quote: HIAS made the bold decision to work in partnership with several other organizations to open a European arm, known as HICEM

claims.quote: In 1965, thanks to the strong advocacy of HIAS and others, U.S. lawmakers replaced the National Origins Act with new legislation

claims.quote: In 2018, HIAS was one of nine agencies contracted by the US State Department to assist refugees.

claims.text: לפי Religion News Service, קבוצות כמו Refugee Resettlement Watch הקדישו שנים להתקפות על הגירה, והמרכז למען החוק הדרומי מסווג אותה כקבוצת שנאה אנטי־מוסלמית.
claims.quote: Groups such as Refugee Resettlement Watch, which runs a blog founded in 2007 that claims 6 million readers, have spent years railing against immigration.

claims.text: לפי יודאיקה, בשנות ה-80 היו מתיחויות בין HIAS לממשלת ישראל בשאלה אם לסייע ליהודי ברית המועצות להגר למדינות שאינן ישראל.

claims.text: לפי האגודה ההיסטורית היהודית האמריקנית, התאריכים המוקדמים (1870–1884) מתייחסים לארגונים דומים שלא היו קודמים אמיתיים של HIAS.
claims.quote: We believe these early dates, in particular 1870-1884, refer to organizations with similar names and missions as HIAS, but which were not true predecessors of HIAS.

claims.text: לפי HIAS, HICEM סייעה ל-250,000 גברים, נשים וילדים להימלט מרדיפות הנאצים.
claims.quote: In the years to come, HICEM would help 250,000 men, women, and children escape Nazi persecution.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית השואה, HIAS דיווחה ב-1944 שסייעה ל-250,000 גברים, נשים וילדים להימלט מרדיפות הנאצים.
claims.quote: In 1944, one year before the end of the war, HIAS reported that it had helped 250,000 men, women, and children escape Nazi persecution.

claims.text: לפי מארק הטפילד, 22 עובדי HIAS נהרגו במהלך המלחמה במילוי תפקידם.
claims.quote: Twenty-two HIAS employees perished during the war in the line of duty.

claims.text: לפי HIAS, החל בשנות ה-90 היא הרחיבה את הושבת הפליטים גם לפליטים לא יהודים מיוגוסלביה לשעבר, מזרח אפריקה, דרום־מזרח אסיה והמזרח התיכון.
claims.quote: HIAS expanded its resettlement work to include assistance to non-Jewish refugees from the former Yugoslavia, East Africa, southeast Asia, and the Middle East.

claims.text: לפי Religion News Service, עד ראשית המאה ה-21 משימתה העיקרית של HIAS הייתה לסייע ליהודים נזקקים.
claims.quote: Until the beginning of the 21st century, its main task had been to assist Jews in need.

claims.text: לפי HIAS, בשנה שלאחר פתיחת פעילותה בקניה היא יצרה את שותפותה הראשונה מזה עשורים עם נציבות האו"ם לפליטים, כדי לסייע לפליטים מאוקראינה.
claims.quote: The following year, HIAS entered into its first partnership in decades with the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, to assist asylum seekers from Ukraine.

claims.text: לפי HIAS, מאז אפריל 2023 יותר מ-12 מיליון איש עקורים בעקבות מלחמת האזרחים בסודאן, ויותר ממיליון סודאנים חצו לצ'אד.
claims.quote: More than 12 million people have been displaced, and more than a million Sudanese have crossed into Chad.

text: HIAS נוסד בניו יורק ב-1881 כדי לעזור ליהודים שברחו מפוגרומים ומעוני במזרח אירופה.
היום אותו ארגון עוזר לפליטים בלי קשר לדת, ללאום או למוצא. בשנת 2025 קלט בארה"ב 3,729 פליטים, ובהם 1,545 מאפגניסטן.
ב-2019 תבע HIAS, יחד עם שני ארגוני קליטה נוספים, את ממשל טראמפ על צו נשיאותי 13888, שנתן למדינות ולרשויות מקומיות זכות וטו על קליטת פליטים. בינואר 2020 שופט פדרלי במרילנד עצר את הצו.
מהימין תוקפים את הארגון בגלל זה. ב-2024 אמר סטיב באנון, לשעבר יועץ של טראמפ, שארגונים כמו HIAS נמצאים שם כדי להחריף את "הפלישה" בגבול הדרומי.
he.opinion: הצלת היהודים מהפוגרומים היא המעשה שבגללו הארגון באתר. הפעילות הפוליטית שלו היום שנויה במחלוקת, ואנחנו לא מאמצים אותה.

text: HIAS was founded in New York in 1881 to help Jews fleeing pogroms and poverty in Eastern Europe.
Today the same organisation helps refugees regardless of religion, nationality or ethnicity. In fiscal 2025 it welcomed 3,729 refugees and visa holders in the US, including 1,545 Afghans.

In 2019 HIAS and two other resettlement agencies sued the Trump administration over Executive Order 13888, which let states and local governments veto refugee resettlement. In January 2020 a federal judge in Maryland blocked the order.
The right attacks HIAS for this. In 2024 Steve Bannon, a former Trump adviser, said groups like HIAS are there to make the "invasion" on the southern border worse.
en.opinion: Saving Jews from the pogroms is the deed this page is about. The organisation's politics today are disputed, and we do not adopt them.
